messages:
Evan Brooks: hi all — first week here. I spun up the repo but my local app keeps timing out connecting to Postgres. Compose shows the db service healthy, bind mount ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data. Error in app: "could not translate host name "db" to address". I'm running the app on host (node) not in container.

Tara V.: welcome Evan! :wave: that error means your app tried to resolve a container hostname. If your app runs on host, use localhost and publish ports in compose (5432:5432). If app will be a service in compose, use the service name (db).

Evan Brooks: ah, I copied DATABASE_URL from .env.example which uses db as host. Quick dumb question: is it safe to publish 5432:5432 on my laptop?

Marta Silva: generally okay for local dev but don't expose in CI or prod. You can restrict to localhost by using "127.0.0.1:5432:5432" in ports if you're worried.

Ken Zhou: FYI on mac M1, bind mounts can cause Postgres to reinit or slow IO. We recommend a named volume for PGDATA and a separate bind mount for migrations/sql if you want host files. Example: volumes:
- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
- ./migrations:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
And set PGDATA env to /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata.

Evan Brooks: great, thanks — I changed compose to expose 127.0.0.1:5432 and updated DATABASE_URL to localhost. App connects now. I'll switch to named volume to avoid reinit.

ops-bot: docs/setup.md auto-updated: "local DB tips: publish ports for host-side apps; prefer named volumes on macOS" (https://git.internal/redwood/docs/setup.md) :white_check_mark:
